node.title: Triple-owner heavy ruling removes common rational poles
node.closure: a three-record-per-pair order-32 packet retains degree at least twenty, excludes pure locators, and makes every denominator-root support incidence singleton
node.statement: In the heavy ruling orientation, pair types owning at most two records cost at most 116722, leaving 322359637 records on triple-owner types. Their common core has size below K-2: otherwise dimension-two shortening caps triple-owner records at 236448715, and restoring all low-multiplicity records gives 236565437, short by 85910922. One triple-owner pair owns at least 5524 records. One anchor and at most four additional pair types recover the common core. Choose three records from every additional pair and 32-3t from the anchor, so at least 20 anchor explanations remain. Core-saturated exact supports have common intersection equal to the recovered core; cancellation gives a nonaffine degree-20-through-31 packet. The partial-relative output is either rational or chi at least 2299571; the two-core root surplus again excludes pure locators. In the rational branch, a common domain pole Q=A=B=0 would lie in at least two supports from every represented pair, hence in every residual pair core, contradicting their empty intersection. Any root of Q lies in at most one selected support, so all denominator-root support incidences are singleton and total at most 67472. No rational or high-complexity payment is claimed.
